use_case: Face verification (1:1) at the county government center employee entrance: the reader compares a live face image with the enrolled template of the badge presented
business_owner: Security Systems Supervisor (for the county, which decides on use)
vendor_or_model: Access control SaaS vendor face verification module (machine learning face matching) with 2 face-capable readers
build_or_buy: Buy (vendor feature, configured by the company)
data_categories: Face templates (biometric data); enrollment photos; badge IDs; match scores; access events
consequential_decision_category: Physical access to a government workplace; physical security of a government facility
human_in_the_loop: Face match is a second factor with the badge. A failed match falls back to badge plus PIN or the guard desk; no one is refused entry on a face result alone
applicable_laws: Fla. Stat. 501.171 (biometric data is personal information; breach notice; reasonable security); Fla. Stat. 119.071(5)(g) (county biometric exemption covers only fingerprints and friction ridge records) and 119.0701 (contractor public records); FTC Act Section 5 (vendor and company claims); county security addendum
status: Pilot continues for enrolled volunteers only, with conditions due 2026-10-31; no new enrollments until conditions are met

consequential_decision_category: Access to essential government services; surveillance of the public
human_in_the_loop: Proposed: alerts to guards; no design for review or appeal
applicable_laws: Fla. Stat. 501.171; Fla. Stat. 119.071 and 119.0701; FTC Act Section 5; county counsel review required
status: Not approved. The company declines to configure or operate it (P01 R-014)
